1. Vide this judgment, I shall dispose of the present appeal preferred by the appellant (accused before the Ld. Trial Court) against the impugned judgment dated 24.01.2024 and order on sentence dated 13.02.2024 in case titled as State Vs 1. Azad Singh,
2. Naveen Maan and 3. Surender Singh, in case FIR no. 276/12 PS Model Town whereby Ld. MM has convicted the accused persons namely Azad Singh and Naveen Maan for the offence punishable under Section 420 r/w 511 IPC and accused Surender was acquitted of the offence under section 420 IPC and accused Azad and accused appellant Naveen were sentenced to undergo imprisonment for the period already undergone by accused persons and fine of Rs. 10,000/- each to be used in defraying the expenses of prosecution DHIRENDRA RANA RANA

Date:
2024.10.09 17:15:19 +0530 and the remaining amount was ordered to be reverted back into the treasury after deduction of expenses in the favour of prosecution.
2. For the sake of convenience, I would be referring the appellant as accused as per the nomenclature before the trial court.

3. The facts in brief as per the chargesheet are that on 21.10.2012, after receipt of DD no. 24 A, SI Lakhmi Chand alongwith SI Kuldeep reached at Govt. Boys Senior Secondary School no. 2, Model Town, Delhi where the Principal of the said school gave his complaint alongwith the complaint of Invigilators, photocopy of sitting plan,
admit card and attendance sheet, two mobile phones alongwith earphones.

Invigilator Ram Bhool caught accused Naveen Maan while he was solving his question papers after asking answers through his mobile phone.
All the three accused were found using unfair means in the examination.
4. On the basis of the said complaint, case FIR no. 276/12 was Naveen Maan Vs State DHIRENDRA Page RANA Date: 2024.10.09 17:15:26 +0530 registered at PS Model Town under section 420/120-B/201 IPC.

sentences.text: During investigation, the admit card, mobile phones, earphones copy of attendance sheet, copy of sitting plan were taken into police possession.
Site plan was prepared and statement of witnesses were recorded.
All the three accused persons were arrested and their disclosure statements were recorded.
The shirts of accused persons which were used for concealing the mobile and ear phones were also taken into police possession.
5. During trial, charge under section 420/120-B/201 IPC was framed against all the accused persons and prosecution examined 12 witnesses in total to prove its case.

6. After conclusion of evidence, separate statement of all three accused persons under section 313 r/w 281 Cr. PC were recorded on 14.02.2023.
7.

After conclusion of the trial, Ld. MM convicted accused Azad Singh and Naveen Maan for the offences under section 420 r/w section 511 IPC and accused Surender was acquitted, vide impugned judgment dated 24.01.2024 and accused Azad Singh and Naveen Maan

were sentenced vide order dated 13.02.2024.
8. Feeling aggrieved by the said impugned judgment and order on sentence, the appellant Naveen Maan has challenged the same on the following grounds :

A. During examination, PW-5 deposed that one candidate DHIRENDRA RANA Date:
2024.10.09 17:15:32 +0530 namely Naveen was not attempting his examination and was sitting idle.
He deposed that on suspicion, he took search of that Naveen and one mobile phone was recovered from his possession.

Thereafter, PW-5 alongwith Ram Bhool took the said candidate Naveen to the Principal office where PW-5 gave the application / complaint to the Principal wherein it is clearly mentioned that one student was found with mobile.
Ld. MM has failed to consider the fact that from the time of initiation of action against Naveen Maan, there is no mention of earphones and such a vital fact was not mentioned in the impugned order.

Moreover, it is also Naveen Maan vs State on 9 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/90489227/
2 clear from the testimony of witness that appellant / accused Naveen was sitting idle and he was not caught while attempting or indulging in any action of cheating.
During the cross examination of PW-5 on behalf of State

entities.text:
Naveen Maan vs State on 9 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/90489227/
2
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: , PW-5 failed to identify accused Naveen Maan as well as the case property i.e. mobile phone and ear phones.

PW-5 also deposed in the said cross examination done on behalf of State that he had not stated to the police that accused had written some answered codes on the question paper and he was using earphone lead for asking those answers.
PW-5 also denied that accused was apprehended in the examination room while he was using mobile phone.
The finding given by Ld. MM that use of mobile phone by accused Naveen has been established, is totally contrary to the evidence available on record.
The witness has categorically denied that any earphone was recovered from the accused.

B. Ld. MM has failed to take note of the fact that while producing the case property,
only two earphones and one broken DHIRENDRA RANA Date:
2024.10.09 17:15:37 +0530 cable was shown to witness PW-5, though the case of the prosecution is that three earphones were recovered.
Hence, the case property also indicates that no earphone was ever recovered from the possession of accused Naveen Maan.

C. The seizure memo has not been signed by any other witness except Ct. Kuldeep and SI Lakhmi Chand whereas six invigilators, one Principal and two persons from SSC were present at the time of time of seizure of case property and the same clearly shows that the IO has manipulated the evidence.
D. Ld.
Trial Court has failed to consider the fact that if accused Naveen has used mobile phone till 3.30 pm, then it is not possible that he could not attempt even a single question.
A glace over the OMR sheet and question paper makes it amply clear that the accused has not been found cheating during the examination.
E. Ld. MM has failed to pen down the material contradictions and discrepancies of star witnesses of prosecution.
F. Ld. MM has failed to appreciate the fact that the material witnesses have failed to identify the accused as well as case property.
9. The evidence recorded before Ld. Trial Court is not being repeated for the sake of brevity in this judgment as same has already been noted down by Ld. Trial Court in the judgment dated 24.01.2024.
This court would deal on the grounds of appeal one by one as relied upon by the appellant.

sentences.text: Ld. Counsel for the appellant has argued on the lines of his appeal and it is prayed that judgment dated 24.01.2024 and order on sentence dated 13.02.2024 be set aside.

11. Per contra, Ld. Addl. PP for the State / respondent submits that there is no illegality or irregularity in the impugned judgment passed by the Ld. Trial Court which needs any interference and the said orders have been passed after due consideration of the material placed on record consisting the testimonies and documents on record.
12.
I have heard Ld. Counsels for the parties and have also considered the material placed on record.
13. It is being argued on behalf of accused that accused Naveen Maan was using the mobile phone when he was apprehended by PW-5.
When this fact is not proved then how come it can be presumed that an attempt of cheating was done by the accused by using a mobile phone.
Further more, PW-5 has failed to identify the accused and the case property.
13.1 It is matter of record that PW-5 has failed to identify the accused but with an explanation that incident pertains to year 2012 and due to lapse of time, he could not identify the accused.
Similarly he also failed to identify the shirt worn by the accused on that day.
The explanation qua non identification of accused has been found to be plausible and justifiable by the Ld. Trial Court and this issue has been dealt with on the basis of evidence and settled law.

It RANA Date:
2024.10.09 17:15:48 +0530 is not the case of the accused that he was not present in the examination hall or that person namely Naveen Maan was some other candidate.
As per the complaint filed by the Principal of GBSSS No. 2, Model Town, accused Naveen Maan having roll no. 2201217841 was found using mobile phone.
It is not the case of the accused that this roll number was not issued to him or he was not appearing in the examination through this roll number.

Therefore, inability of PW-5 to identify the accused is of no consequence as his presence and identification is duly proved on the basis of documentary evidence which is not in question by any stretch of imagination.
14. PW-5 was not alone witness in whose presence accused was apprehended from Room no. 104 when he was using the mobile phone in the examination hall.
Prosecution has examined the second invigilator in that room namely Sh. Ram Bhool as PW-7.
I have minutely gone through the testimony of this witness and he has thoroughly supported the case of prosecution.
He was on duty with PW-5 Avdesh Kumar and he has categorically stated that accused Naveen was using mobile phone and earphones during the examination.
Similar was his statement given to the IO under section 161 Cr. PC.

He deposed before the court that he alongwith PW-5 Avdesh Kumar Singh took accused Naveen alongwih the recovered mobile phone to the office of Principal and briefed the Naveen Maan vs State on 9 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/90489227/
4 Principal about the recovery of mobile phone and earphone from accused Naveen Maan.

sentences.text: PW-5 Avdesh Kumar Singh gave a written complaint to the Principal which was also signed by PW-7 Ram Naveen Maan Vs State PageRANA RANA Date: 2024.10.09 17:15:53 +0530 Bhool.

entities.text: Ram Naveen Maan Vs State PageRANA RANA
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Although, PW-7 is not able to identify the accused due to lapse of time but his testimony is clear and unequivocal to the effect that accused was found using the mobile phone with the help of an earphone.

Therefore,
the confusion created by PW-5 qua the fact whether accused Naveen was found using the mobile phone or not or whether he was found in possession of any earphone or not, has been clarified by PW-7.
He has been cross examined on behalf of accused but there is not a single suggestion to rebut the fact that accused was not found using the mobile phone with the help of an earphone.
15. Law is settled that a person can be convicted on the basis of a sole testimony provided it is trustworthy, credible and free from all kind of criticism.
No particular number of witnesses are required to be examined to prove any allegation against the accused.
Needless to say, it is the quality of witness rather than the quantity which is to be considered by the court while appreciating the evidence adduced by the parties.

Testimony of PW-7 Ram Bhool inspires confidence of this court and in absence of any suggestion on the part of the accused to the effect that he was not using the mobile phone or earphone was not recovered from his possession, this fact is duly proved by the prosecution against the accused beyond reasonable doubt.

Therefore, the focus laid down by Ld.
Defence Counsel on the testimony of PW-5
is misconceived in the light of testimony of PW-7 who was also present as an invigilator in the said room.
16. Similar is the status of argument that witnesses could not

DHIRENDRA RANA RANA Date:
2024.10.09 17:15:57 +0530 identify the earphone allegedly recovered from the possession of the accused.

IO had prepared only one seizure memo of all three earphones and two mobile phones recovered from the possession of accused Naveen,
Azad and Surender.

Ideally, IO should have seized the mobile phones and earphones recovered from each accused vide separate seizure memo to avoid any confusion but if that is not done then it is a mere irregularity which does not go to the roots of the case.
The issue before the court is whether accused was found using mobile phone for the purpose of cheating or not.
Law is settled that if any lacuna is left in the investigation, then the entire case of the prosecution cannot be disbelieved which is otherwise proved.
In the present case, it has been proved by the testimony of PW-7 that accused Naveen was found using the mobile phone and earphone in the examination hall.
PW-5 has proved the fact that one person namely Naveen was apprehended from Room no. 104, although he could not identify the accused and recovered mobile phone and earphone.
As stated above, it is not in dispute that accused Naveen was not appearing in the examination in Room no. 104 on the said date.
17. Prosecution has proved the fact that accused Naveen was using the mobile phone with the help of his call detail records.

Ld. Trial Court has rightly observed that mobile SIM recovered from possession of accused Naveen was issued in the name of his father and accused did receive phone calls on the said number from 2.00 pm to 4.00 pm on that day.

There is no explanation available Naveen Maan vs State on 9 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/90489227/
5 with the accused on what account he had these calls during the Naveen Maan Vs State DHIRENDRA RANA RANA Date:
2024.10.09 17:16:02 +0530 examination time of 2.00 pm to 4.00 pm.

sentences.text: Therefore, on the basis of CDR, it is proved by the prosecution that accused Naveen was using the said mobile phone while appearing in the examination.

18. It is also argued on behalf of accused that seizure memo of the mobile phone and earphone ought to have been signed by the independent witnesses instead of police officials which raises the presumption of manipulation of case property in this case.

As stated above, IO could have cited the officials present at the examination centre as witness in the seizure memo but if that is not done,
then it has no bearing on the merits of this case.
The fact remains the same that accused Naveen Maan was using the mobile phone and earphone and he was detected and apprehended by PW-5 and PW-7.
Absence of signature of any invigilator or Principal on the seizure memo is not a significant issue which can be considered by the court to disbelieve the case of the prosecution.
19. It is also argued that accused had not attempted any question till 3.30 pm.
If he was using the mobile phone and was receiving the answers from outside, then he could have and should have attempted the exam.
This is a hypothetical argument raised on behalf of accused.
Why accused did not attempt any question is in the knowledge of the accused only and nobody else can disclose the same.
If this aspect is considered otherwise, then accused should have something in his mind and that is why he did not attempt a single question till 3.30 pm.

Meaning thereby, he was sure enough to get the answers telephonically but unfortunately, he was RANA Date:
2024.10.09 17:16:14 +0530 apprehended by the invigilators before he could receive the complete answer key and fill the same in the OMR sheet.
Therefore, this argument is again of no consequence and holds no water and accordingly, stands rejected.

20. Considering the above discussion and materiel available on record, this court is of the considered view that Trial Court has rightly convicted accused Naveen Maan for an attempt of cheating which is punishable under section 420 r/w 511 IPC.

The judgment passed by Ld. Trial Court is well reasoned and based upon settled law and interference of this court is not required for any purpose.
21.

As far as order on sentence is concerned, no interference is required as already a lenient view has been taken against the accused and he has been punished to undergo simple imprisonment for the period already undergone by him in custody and to pay a fine of Rs. 10,000/-.
22.
Accordingly, the present appeal stands dismissed.
The impugned judgment dated 24.01.2024 and order on sentence dated 13.02.2024 are upheld.
